'''Connie Barbara Roth''' (born 1974){{r|loc}} is a Canadian-American [[soft matter]] physicist and [[Polymer science|polymer scientist]] whose research concerns the [[glass transition]] and aging in [[Plastic film|polymer films]].{{r|tv|faps}} She is a professor of physics at [[Emory University]].

==Education and career==
Roth became interested in physics as a teenager in [[Toronto]] through the [[MacGyver]] television show, and began her interest in polymer films through studying paper and [[toner (printing)|toner]] in a summer internship at the [[Xerox]] Research Centre of Canada.{{r|tv}} She studied physics as an undergraduate at [[McMaster University]] in Ontario,{{r|about}} graduating in 1997.{{r|orcid}} She went to the [[University of Guelph]], also in Ontario, for graduate study in physics,{{r|about}} earning a master's degree in 1999{{r|loc}} and completing her Ph.D. in 2004.{{r|bios}}

After postdoctoral research at [[Simon Fraser University]] in British Columbia and [[Northwestern University]] in Chicago, Roth joined the Emory University faculty in 2007. She was promoted to associate professor in 2013 and full professor in 2021.{{r|about}}

==Recognition==
Roth was named as a [[Fellow of the American Physical Society]] (APS) in 2019, after a nomination from the APS Division of Polymer Physics, "for exceptional contributions to the understanding of glass transition and aging phenomena in polymer films and blends".{{r|faps}} She was the 2019 recipient of the Fellows Award of the North American Thermal Analysis Society.{{r|natas}}
